panels.title: Status at a Glance
panels.description: Start here. Overall Health covers the daemon's feed, workers, and overlay freshness. Active Alerts covers dependent services, quotas, workflows, and external checks. Green daemon health does not override a firing alert.

panels.title: Overall Health
panels.description: Core daemon runtime health only. HEALTHY means the market-data feed, worker threads, and overlay output are healthy. It does not include provider quotas, workflow results, credentials, or external integrations; review Active Alerts for those systems. IDLE means the market is closed before the first bar.

panels.title: Active Alerts
panels.description: Currently firing Grafana alerts for live overlay, collector, and dependent services.

panels.title: Incident Triage Guide
panels.description: Suggested first checks when Overall Health is not HEALTHY.

options.content:
**Incident triage**

1. Check **Active Alerts** first.
2. If **Feed Healthy** is red: check Databento credentials, feed reconnects, and Railway logs.
3. If **Workers Healthy** is red: open Worker Liveness and restart the daemon if a worker is dead.
4. If **Overlay Fresh** is red: check Compute Cycle Errors and Overlay & Bar Age.
5. If internal API traffic is missing while **Market Status** is open: check authorized server-side consumers, auth denied, and request rate.
6. If dashboards show no data: check Collector / Scrape Targets.

Runbook: [README](https://github.com/skipp-dev/skipp-algo/blob/main/services/live_overlay_daemon/README.md)
7. If **Signal Pipeline Ready** is red: check **Open-Prep Snapshot**, **Watchlist Symbols**, **Producer Poll Age**, then Collector / Scrape Targets and signals-producer Railway logs.

---
**Quick links** · [Railway logs](https://railway.com/project/0616a3b7-7b7f-41d1-8fac-a0b8922c94ca/service/705582c5-ba8b-4c6e-848c-33bffe0a61b0/logs?environmentId=470fbd0f-894d-46cd-8722-6b072d255d99) · [Railway deployments](https://railway.com/project/0616a3b7-7b7f-41d1-8fac-a0b8922c94ca/service/705582c5-ba8b-4c6e-848c-33bffe0a61b0/deployments?environmentId=470fbd0f-894d-46cd-8722-6b072d255d99) · [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/skipp-dev/skipp-algo/actions) · [Runbook: live-overlay on-call](https://github.com/skipp-dev/skipp-algo/blob/main/services/live_overlay_daemon/OPS.md)

panels.title: Market Status
panels.description: Major session state (US regular or Europe regular); 1 = open, 0 = closed.

panels.title: External Consumer Watchdog
panels.description: Whether this deployment expects an external client to call /smc_live during the US regular market session. NO CONSUMER EXPECTED is the correct current state; CONSUMER EXPECTED arms missing-traffic alerts after a verified client rollout.

panels.title: Core Metrics Present
panels.description: Can Grafana still see the service? This panel turns red when the core daemon metric series disappear, which usually means the process is down or the scrape target is unreachable.

panels.title: External Checks
panels.description: External bridge scrape health (UptimeRobot + GitHub Workflows).

panels.title: Deployed build (commit @ branch)
panels.description: The commit + branch currently running in the daemon, from live_overlay_build_info. 'unknown' means a deploy without a git stamp (e.g. bare railway up). Use it to confirm a deploy actually shipped the intended commit.

panels.title: Trading Evidence and Promotion Readiness
panels.description: Evidence needed before a signal family can advance: valid sample counts toward the 40-sample floor, evidence freshness, and paper-trading activity.

panels.title: Valid Samples by Signal Family
panels.description: Usable scored samples with a triggered return for each signal family. A family needs at least 40 samples before evaluation. Break of Structure is the active candidate; Sweep is still a proof of concept, while Fair Value Gap and Order Block are controls.

panels.title: Magnitude Ledger Age (days)
panels.description: Age of the newest magnitude evidence row. Red at 5 days, matching the alert budget for a weekday producer plus weekends and holidays. Row count, candidate passes, and the newest evaluation plane are context only and have no age threshold.

panels.title: Evidence Data Availability
panels.description: 1 = the corresponding evidence date is known/parseable, 0 = unknown (snapshot missing that field). Guards against a stale age reading 0 being mistaken for fresh.

panels.title: GitHub Crons — Newest Run (agg)
panels.description: Aggregate across all monitored workflows: age and duration of the single newest run the daemon has seen. A large age here means the whole GitHub-Actions cron fleet has gone quiet (complements the per-workflow rules).

panels.title: Paper-Trading Fill Activity
panels.description: Operational activity of the paper-trading pipeline: closed and filled records across all incubations. This confirms the execution path is alive; it is not the per-family promotion sample gate shown above.

panels.title: Evidence Chain Age (days)
panels.description: Raw age in days for each evidence output. Reference budgets are: ledger 5 days, audit branch 4 days, walk-forward summary 7 days, and freshness snapshot 1 day. The lines show age, not percentage of budget consumed.

panels.title: Live Data Chain (Feed → Overlay → Pine)
panels.description: The market-data path end to end: Databento feed → overlay computation → TradingView/Pine polling. A break here stops signals reaching users.

panels.title: Feed Healthy
panels.description: Live feed connection health (0 = unhealthy, 1 = healthy).

panels.title: Last Bar Age
panels.description: Age of the newest bar received from Databento.

panels.title: Overlay Fresh
panels.description: Is the latest overlay calculation recent enough to trade on? Green means the last computed overlay is within the expected freshness window.

panels.title: Market Data Freshness
panels.description: Are market-open bars still arriving on time? Shows freshness SLO over the last hour.

panels.title: External Consumer Traffic

targets.expr: max((live_overlay_market_us_open{job=~"$job"} or on() vector(0)) + ((live_overlay_market_us_open{job=~"$job"} or on() vector(0)) * (live_overlay_expected_market_traffic{job=~"$job"} or on() vector(0))) + ((live_overlay_market_us_open{job=~"$job"} or on() vector(0)) * (live_overlay_expected_market_traffic{job=~"$job"} or on() vector(0)) * (((rate(live_overlay_smc_live_requests_total{job=~"$job"}[5m]) or on() vector(0)) > bool 0.001))))

panels.description: Whether a verified external client is expected to call /smc_live, and whether requests are arriving during the US regular market session. NO CONSUMER EXPECTED is healthy while the endpoint has no deployed client. This is API traffic only.

panels.title: Overlay Symbols
panels.description: Number of distinct symbols currently held in the in-memory SMC overlay cache.

panels.title: Bar Symbols
panels.description: Number of distinct symbols with at least one 1-minute bar in the ingest cache.

panels.title: Bar Count
panels.description: Total 1-minute bars currently retained across all symbols.

panels.title: Signal Pipeline Ready
panels.description: 1 = healthy: watchlist loaded, Open-Prep snapshot present, and a poll succeeded within the last 5 minutes. Age=0 is treated as not-ready. 0 = pipeline not ready.

targets.expr: (   (signals_producer_watchlist_symbols{job=~"signals_producer"} > bool 0) * (signals_producer_open_prep_snapshot_loaded{job=~"signals_producer"} > bool 0) * ((signals_producer_last_poll_age_seconds{job=~"signals_producer"} or on() vector(999999)) < bool 300) ) or on() vector(0)

panels.title: Open-Prep Snapshot
panels.description: 1 = Open-Prep snapshot loaded; 0 = missing.

panels.title: Watchlist Symbols
panels.description: Number of symbols loaded into the realtime signal watchlist.

panels.title: Producer Poll Age
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful realtime signal poll completed (age=0 before first poll).

panels.title: Producer FMP Bandwidth
panels.description: Five-minute rate of Financial Modeling Prep traffic from the continuously running signals producer. Bytes per second measures decoded response volume; requests per second measures call frequency. Counters restart when the service restarts.

panels.title: Extended-Hours Feed Shadow
panels.description: Shadow-only comparison of FMP's regular batch quote with the dedicated aftermarket quote and trade feeds. Fresh trade prices win; a fresh non-crossed bid/ask midpoint is the fallback. Signal-ready additionally requires a same-session regular-close cumulative-volume baseline. No extended-hours signal is published from this probe.

panels.title: Global Market Sessions
panels.description: Regular trading session state for US, Europe, and Asia markets.

panels.title: Overlay & Bar Age
panels.description: Time since the overlay cache and the newest ingested bar were last refreshed.

panels.title: Feed Health Counters
panels.description: Feed-level counters: reconnects, Databento errors, unexpected errors, circuit breakers and partial restarts.

panels.title: Compute Cycle Errors
panels.description: Rate of errors raised during SMC overlay compute cycles (full + flow refresh).

panels.title: Overlay API Reliability
panels.description: How reliably the live-overlay API serves authenticated client requests: success rate, latency against the service target, and error-budget consumption. Service-owner detail.

panels.title: Success Rate (%)
panels.description: Percentage of recent /smc_live overlay HTTP requests (from Pine/TradingView) that completed successfully. Shows NO REQUESTS when none are observed.

panels.title: Request Latency Against 500 ms Target
panels.description: Five-minute request latency at the 95th and 99th percentiles, compared with the fixed 500 millisecond service target.

panels.title: Error Budget Burn Rate
panels.description: Rate of bad events over 5m/30m/1h/6h windows used for multi-window SLO alerting.

panels.title: Request Rate
panels.description: HTTP request rate to the daemon endpoints as observed by Grafana Alloy.

panels.title: Failure Mix
panels.description: Breakdown of compute/feed failures by category over time.

panels.title: Stale Budget Consumed (%)
panels.description: How much of the configured max_stale budget is currently consumed. 100 % means the overlay is at the stale threshold. This is derived from overlay_age_seconds / max_stale_seconds.

panels.title: Stale Responses (served)
panels.description: Count of health/status responses served while the overlay or feed data was stale.

panels.title: Daemon Operations
panels.description: Process health of the overlay daemon: restarts and their causes, worker liveness, memory, ingest-queue backpressure and hotspots. Service-owner detail.

panels.title: Service Status
panels.description: Daemon lifecycle state: UNKNOWN, STARTING, IDLE or OK. Combines feed readiness, worker liveness, overlay freshness and market-open context.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Daemon process uptime since the last start/restart.

panels.title: Process Resident Memory
panels.description: Daemon process resident memory as reported by the built-in Prometheus collector.

panels.title: Workers Healthy
panels.description: Background thread liveness (1 = all alive, 0 = at least one dead).

panels.title: Feed Circuit Breakers (Total)
panels.description: Cumulative number of times the feed circuit breaker opened since process start.

panels.title: Feed Partial Restarts (Total)
panels.description: Cumulative number of partial feed restarts (lighter than a full reconnect).

panels.title: Daemon Restarts (24h)
panels.description: Estimated number of daemon restarts in the last 24 hours based on uptime resets.

panels.title: Worker Liveness
panels.description: Per-worker thread liveness: live_feed, overlay_refresh, flow_refresh, ingest_processor.

panels.title: Readiness Components Timeline
panels.description: Readiness components over time: feed healthy, workers healthy, overlay fresh, market open.

panels.title: Restart Causes (24h)
panels.description: Restart cause distribution over the last 24 hours, counted as start-time changes of live_overlay_daemon_start_time_seconds per cause (the per-cause _total counters are reset to 1 each process, so increase() over them was always 0).

panels.title: Ingest Queue Backpressure
panels.description: Current ingest queue depth versus its configured maximum (left axis) and the rate of dropped messages (right axis).

panels.title: Ingest Queue Lag (ms)
panels.description: End-to-end latency from bar arrival to ingestion completion.

panels.title: Most Requested Symbols
panels.description: Per-symbol /smc_live request rate for the selected time range. Empty means no external client requests were observed, not a dashboard failure.

panels.title: Most Requested Timeframes
panels.description: Per-timeframe /smc_live request rate for the selected time range. Empty means no external client requests were observed, not a dashboard failure.

panels.title: External Checks and Automation
panels.description: Health of GitHub workflows, uptime monitors, and the bridges that import their status. Service-owner detail.

panels.title: GitHub Workflow Bridge

targets.expr:
max by (job) (live_overlay_bridge_enabled{job=~"$job",bridge="github_workflow"})
+ on(job)
max by (job) (live_overlay_bridge_scrape_success{job=~"$job",bridge="github_workflow"})
or on() vector(0)

panels.description: Is the daemon successfully SCRAPING the GitHub-Actions workflow monitor? OK = scraped & healthy · SCRAPE ERROR = configured but the scrape is failing · DISABLED = monitor not configured. (This is the monitoring bridge itself — actual workflow pass/fail is in the panels below.)

panels.title: GitHub Workflow Bridge Error
panels.description: Last scrape error from the GitHub-Actions workflow monitoring bridge (OK = none).

panels.title: GitHub Workflow Snapshot Age
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful GitHub workflow bridge poll.

panels.title: Bridge Metrics Present
panels.description: Counts how many of the generic bridge contracts are absent. A non-zero value means the exporter or metrics path is broken, not that a bridge is disabled.

panels.title: UptimeRobot Bridge

targets.expr:
max by (job) (live_overlay_bridge_enabled{job=~"$job",bridge="uptimerobot"})
+ on(job)
max by (job) (live_overlay_bridge_scrape_success{job=~"$job",bridge="uptimerobot"})
or on() vector(0)

panels.description: Is the daemon successfully SCRAPING the UptimeRobot monitor? OK = scraped & healthy · SCRAPE ERROR = configured but failing · DISABLED = not configured. (Individual monitor states are in the panels below.)

panels.title: UptimeRobot Bridge Error
panels.description: Last scrape error from the UptimeRobot monitoring bridge (OK = none).

panels.title: UptimeRobot Snapshot Age
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful UptimeRobot bridge poll.

panels.title: GitHub Workflow Runs
panels.description: Snapshot counts of GitHub workflow runs by phase from the latest bridge scrape.

panels.title: UptimeRobot Monitors
panels.description: UptimeRobot actual/allowlist-expected counts, up/down status, and response time.

panels.title: GitHub Workflows — Latest Run Detail
panels.description: Per-workflow detail of the most recent run the daemon observed: trigger event (schedule / push / …), current status, run duration and age. One row per named workflow. Driven by the labelled live_overlay_github_workflow_* gauges (phase_code, latest_duration_seconds, latest_age_seconds, latest_success).

panels.title: Bridge Scrape Health Timeline
panels.description: External bridge scrape health over time (UptimeRobot + GitHub Workflows). DISABLED = bridge not configured; SCRAPE ERROR = configured but failing; OK = healthy.

panels.title: UptimeRobot Monitor States
panels.description: Per-monitor UptimeRobot state over time. paused = monitor intentionally paused; unknown = unrecognized status code.

panels.title: GitHub Workflow Status — Timeline
panels.description: Colour-coded latest status of each GitHub Actions workflow over time. Every row is one named workflow ({{workflow}} legend); the cell colour encodes the run conclusion — green=success, red=failure/timed-out/startup-failure, orange=cancelled/action-required, blue=in-progress/neutral, yellow=queued/stale, gray=unknown, purple=skipped. Series come from live_overlay_github_workflow_phase_code{workflow,event,workflow_id}, sampled at the daemon's GitHub workflow bridge interval (so runs shorter than one scrape interval may not appear).

panels.title: Providers (Feeds, News & Credentials)
panels.description: Upstream data providers: Databento market-data feed + FMP + TradingView credential/delivery health, and news ingest state. (Databento feed VOLUME — bars/symbols — is in the Live Data Chain section.) Service-owner detail.

panels.title: Estimated FMP Quota Used (%)
panels.description: Estimated Financial Modeling Prep quota pressure. The numerator combines the calendar-month ingest snapshot with the signals producer's rolling 30-day response volume, so this is an operational estimate rather than the provider's billing meter. Warning starts at 80% and critical at 95%; verify the provider portal before changing plans.

panels.title: Estimated FMP Usage
panels.description: Estimated Financial Modeling Prep data volume, auto-scaled from bytes. It combines the calendar-month ingest snapshot with the signals producer's rolling 30-day volume; the two time windows make this a conservative operational estimate, not an invoice value.

panels.title: Databento API Key
panels.description: Is the Databento market-data API key valid? (The feed itself — bars/symbols/queue — is in the Live Data Chain section.)

panels.title: Databento Delivery Age
panels.description: Days since the configured Databento delivery probe last reported market data (DBEQ.BASIC). Good < 3d; a growing gap means the feed is falling behind. If no delivery probe is configured or its credential-health snapshot is unavailable, this shows NOT CONFIGURED.

panels.title: FMP API Key
panels.description: Whether the Financial Modeling Prep credential is accepted by the provider. Quota pressure and measured data volume are shown in the estimated usage panels above.

panels.title: Provider Data Volume (this month)
panels.description: Cumulative data volume (bytes, auto-scaled) consumed per REST provider this month, from the ingest usage snapshot. FMP is the metered one (150 GB quota); Benzinga/UW shown for context. Databento (streaming feed) volume is in the Live Data Chain section (bar counts).

panels.title: TradingView Credential Status
panels.description: Whether the latest credential-health report considers the TradingView storage-state login valid (severity not error). 1 = valid (cached login still within the 72h TTL), 0 = expired/error → re-capture TV_STORAGE_STATE. NOT LOADED means the credential-health report has not loaded yet.

panels.title: TradingView Credential Age
panels.description: Hours since the TradingView Playwright storage-state login (meta.authValidatedAt) was last validated, from the daily credential-health report (tv_storage_state_age probe). Policy TTL is 72h: green < 57.6h (80% warn band), yellow 57.6–72h, red once the cached login is older than 72h and must be re-captured. NOT LOADED means the credential-health report has not loaded yet.

panels.title: Benzinga/Massive API Key
panels.description: Is the configured Benzinga/Massive news API key valid? Load-bearing since 2026-07-08 (open_prep Core News lane + hourly live-news cron). If the provider is not configured or its credential-health snapshot is unavailable, this shows NOT CONFIGURED.

panels.title: GitHub PAT
panels.description: Is GH_PAT valid? Used by every workflow that opens auto-PRs, publishes rolling bot snapshots, or refreshes the TV cookie.

panels.title: GitHub PAT Days Left
panels.description: Days until GH_PAT expiry (from the token's expiration header). Blank/NO EXPIRY for a no-expiry or fine-grained PAT without a returned expiry.

panels.title: Finnhub API Key
panels.description: Is the Finnhub API key valid? Optional provider (terminal_finnhub / open_prep macro). Shows NO DATA until FINNHUB_API_KEY is configured — the probe self-skips when the key is unset.

panels.title: Provider Rate-Limit Hits (429s, this month)
panels.description: HTTP 429 (rate-limit) hits per provider this month, counted in newsstack_fmp/_bz_http.py. The vendors send no X-RateLimit-* headers, so this is the only throttling signal -- a rising line means ingest is brushing the provider's rate limit (retries usually absorb it). Empty until a 429 occurs.

panels.title: News Provider State Codes
panels.description: Legend for News Provider panels directly below.

options.content: **News provider state codes:** `0` = unknown / no data, `1` = degraded, `2` = ok, `3` = disabled (not ingested). The **News Providers — Ingest Status & Reason** table shows the human-readable reason (e.g. API key missing, no active subscription, provider disabled) and whether each provider is actually consumed.

panels.title: News Providers — State Code
panels.description: Per-provider news state code: 0=unknown, 1=degraded, 2=ok, 3=disabled (not ingested).

panels.title: News Provider Health State
panels.description: Aggregate news provider health flags (ok / degraded / unknown).

panels.title: News Snapshot Age
panels.description: Age of the smc_live_news_snapshot.json provider state.

panels.title: News Provider Counts
panels.description: Aggregate provider counts (ok/degraded/unknown/disabled/consumed).

panels.title: News Providers — OK/Degraded (Drill-down)
panels.description: Per-provider ok/degraded/unknown state codes over time.

panels.title: News Providers — Ingest Status & Reason
panels.description: Per-provider ingest status with the human-readable degraded reason (API key missing, no active subscription, provider disabled, …) and whether the provider is actually consumed.

panels.title: Infrastructure (Railway / Collector)
panels.description: Where the daemon runs: Railway CPU/memory/disk/network and the metrics collector scrape targets. Service-owner detail.

panels.title: Railway Metrics Bridge
panels.description: Whether the Railway metrics bridge is enabled and its last poll succeeded.

targets.expr:
(
  max by (job) (live_overlay_bridge_enabled{job=~"$job",bridge="railway_metrics"})
  +
  max by (job) (live_overlay_bridge_scrape_success{job=~"$job",bridge="railway_metrics"})
)
or on(job) label_replace(vector(0), "job", "live_overlay", "", "")

panels.title: Railway Metrics Snapshot Age
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful Railway metrics poll.

panels.title: Railway Metrics Error
panels.description: Latest Railway metrics bridge error class. OK when healthy.

panels.title: Railway CPU Cores
panels.description: CPU cores used per Railway service (from Railway GraphQL metrics).

panels.title: Railway Memory Used Ratio
panels.description: Memory usage / memory limit per Railway service.

panels.title: Railway Memory Limit (GB)
panels.description: Memory limit per Railway service in GB.

panels.title: Railway Disk Usage (GB)
panels.description: Disk usage per Railway service in GB. Railway may omit DISK_USAGE_GB; if no series is shown while Railway Metrics Bridge is OK, disk data is unavailable rather than scraped as zero.

panels.title: Railway Network RX (GB)
panels.description: Network receive (RX) per Railway service in GB.

panels.title: Railway Network TX (GB)
panels.description: Network transmit (TX) per Railway service in GB.

panels.title: Service Metrics Present
panels.description: Presence of the canonical health/watchlist metrics for the remote-write services. This intentionally does not use Prometheus up: up only exists for pull-scraped targets and is empty when these services publish through remote_write.

panels.title: Collector Resident Memory
panels.description: Resident memory for Alloy, signals_producer and live_overlay jobs. live_overlay and signals_producer expose prefixed metric names.

panels.title: Pine Library ↔ TradingView Versions
panels.description: Repo↔TradingView Pine-library version drift (#3599/#3603). Each SMC_*.pine consumer pins import preuss_steffen/<lib>/<N>; this section shows where N no longer matches the real published TradingView version. Drift here is what caused CE10272 on every modern mp.* symbol after micro_profiles sat at /1 vs a live /152 for ~4 months. Fix: repin the offending consumers.

panels.title: Pine consumers drifted from published TV version
panels.description: sum of live_overlay_pine_consumer_drift — a repo import pin (import preuss_steffen/<lib>/<N>) whose N != the real published TradingView version (the #3599/#3603 failure mode: micro_profiles /1 vs /152). 0 = all pins current.

panels.title: Pine consumer pins vs published TradingView version
panels.description: Per-consumer import-pin drift. Value=1 means an SMC_*.pine consumer pins import preuss_steffen/<library>/<N> at an N != the real published version. Sourced from pine_library_version_bridge (bot/live-pine-library-versions).

panels.title: Pine library data freshness
panels.description: Age of ASOF_DATE inside pine/generated/smc_micro_profiles_generated.pine. This is the data watermark used by the SMC Long-Dip Suite warning label; it is independent of snapshot heartbeat and published-version drift.

panels.title: TradingView Dropdown Bindings
panels.description: Live status of saved Pine source hashes and measured input.source assignments published by the scheduled read-only verifier.

panels.title: TradingView Binding Status
panels.description: Latest TradingView saved-source and dropdown-binding verification. Healthy means the snapshot loaded, all 8 saved Pine sources match the repo, all 108 bindings were checked, the snapshot is less than 24 hours old, and both drift and mismatch counts are zero.
